summary: Kootenai NF lookout in Lincoln County, MT: CCC-erected steel tower of 1935 with a 1928 ground house and a 1940 ground cabin, listed on NHLR in 2000; current staffing and access are not confirmed.

facts.design: Steel tower with 7x7-ft metal cab, erected by the CCC in 1935

access.note: Reached by a forest road that a travel blog describes as steep and rough, worsening in the last two miles; no current access status was found in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Travel blog reports driving most of the way up the forest road and walking to the tower; the post is undated

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest (Libby Ranger District, cooperator)

events.note: Begun as a crow's nest tree lookout; NHLR says the site was used as a lookout point in the early 1920s
One-room residence ground house (firelookout.com calls it a frame cabin of living quarters)
Steel tower with 7x7-ft metal cab erected by the CCC; height 72 ft per firelookout.com, 80 ft per NHLR
New ground house or ground cabin constructed
Date registered per NHLR detail page: May 12, 2000
Ground cabin torn down; the tower remained

One of four Kootenai NF assessments, done by association volunteers, to set restoration priorities for the next season. PDF text could not be machine-quoted (duplicated lines), so no evidence quote is given for this event.

corrections.proposed: 1935 built (CCC steel tower with 7x7-ft cab); 1940 new ground house or cabin
corrections.why: Both the NHLR and firelookout.com date the steel tower to 1935. The 1940 date is for the ground house or cabin, not the tower.

corrections.current: One of four Libby District assessments that set the 2021 priorities

corrections.why: The 2020 projects PDF says four assessments were done on the Kootenai NF for next season's restoration priorities. The Libby District and 2021 wording does not appear in the text I could read; the PDF could not be quote-checked because its extracted lines are duplicated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives a 72-ft steel tower (21.9 m, matching the record's height_m); NHLR gives 80 ft (about 24.4 m). The record keeps 21.9 m, which matches one source. The editor should decide which to use.
NHLR gives 5,978 ft (1,822 m) and firelookout.com gives 6040 ft. The record keeps NHLR's 1822.1 m. The story gives no specific figure.
The two sources agree the steel tower dates to 1935 and the 1940 work was a ground house or cabin. The record's 1940 'built' event is the ground cabin.

notes_for_editor: Blue Mountain (Kootenai NF, Libby) is a different site from other Blue Mountain lookouts in Montana, so keep the Libby identity and the NHLR number US 342, MT 24. Height conflicts (72 vs 80 ft). Current staffing and access are unconfirmed: firelookout.com is undated and describes summer staffing, and a travel blog with no visible date describes a host trailer and a rough road. The Kootenai camping-and-cabins page excerpt I read does not list Blue Mountain, but the list was partial, so rental status is left unstated. No notable fire at the site appears in these sources. The 2020 PDF could not be quote-checked because its extracted text is duplicated, so the 2020 assessment is in events without a quote.
